v.why: Replacing a weak pooling edge with a 3x3 conv gives a large gain (experiment 1: +6 to +12 points).
Restoring the input edge with a conv, instead of swapping one op for another, gives a big gain (experiment 16: +5 to +16 points).
Adding a conv on the direct input-to-output edge where there was none adds a useful path, more than replacing an existing op would.
Experiments 6 and 13 show that adding a pooling edge where the edge was none, in a sparse cell, hurts by 6 to 13 points.
With the input edge 0 removed, making edge 3 a pooling edge leaves a weak cell, as in experiment 6 (about -12 points).
Swapping the direct-edge pooling for a skip connection helps (experiment 20: +4.7 to +6.6 points).
Downgrading a 3x3 conv to a 1x1 conv loses capacity (experiments 18 and 19: negative on all three datasets).
Replacing pooling with a skip connection improves gradient flow and accuracy (experiment 2: +1.2 to +6.8 points).
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a skip connection loses learned capacity, so the edit is worse than when replacing a weaker op.
Replacing a pooling edge with a conv gives a consistent gain on all three datasets (experiment 14: about +3.3 points each).

raw:

I ran no further experiments to test them. Hypotheses 9 and 10 rest on weak or single-experiment evidence, so they are the least certain.
